items.title: v0.7.0
items.abstract_or_text: ## Overview llama.cpp v0.7.0 adds the LiliCorr speculative decoding technique and MTP for GLM5-Next, a new GPU cache for MoE experts kept in host memory (`--moe-cache-mib`, up to ~2.2x decode speedup when experts are offloaded), and a large batch of new models: K2 Horizon (dense and MoVA), Prism Bonsai 2 27B, EmbeddingGemma-2 (text+vision+audio), the LiquidAI d1/d1-omni and vLLM decision 2/d3 decision models, pplx-decider, MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL / Nemotron Bolt and maion-coder. The server gets a refactored chat session API (`common_chat_session`, part-based formatted output), much better slot and prompt-cache restore behavior, decision-model support for the new architectures and a new default port (9931), the web UI gains a full models manager, and ggml is updated to v0.27.0. ### Highlights - New GPU cache for host-memory MoE experts (`--moe-cache-mib`): experts run on the GPU from an LRU cache, up to 2.2x faster decode [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887) - The expert cache is now shared across multiple GPUs [#30112](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30112) - LiliCorr speculative decoding: candidate selection with a small draft transformer on top of DFlash [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506) - GLM5-Next: MTP speculative decoding with an optimized sparse attention path [#29928](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29928) - K2 Horizon support in both dense and MoVA variants: conversion, tokenizer, chat template, `-sm tensor` splitting [#29535](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29535) - Prism Bonsai 2 27B ternary model support [#29600](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29600) - EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embedding model [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054) - New decision models: LiquidAI d1-3B, d1-omni-600M, vLLM decision 2, vLLM d3 and pplx-decider [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114) [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383) [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044) - PLaMo-3 tokenizer implements reference pre-segmentation for exact tokenization parity [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045) - RPC server supports `-sm tensor` (tensor-parallel RPC, RPC protocol v8) [#26610](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26610) - Server now listens on port 9931 by default instead of 8080 [#30159](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30159) ### API changes - `include/llama.h`: new `moe_cache_size` context param for the host-expert GPU cache [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887) - `include/llama.h`: new `LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_PLAMO3` vocab type [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045) - `include/llama.h`: `llama_perf_context_data` reports graph reallocations during inference [#30329](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30329) - `include/llama.h`: `embeddings` now skips the LM head when a pooling type other than NONE is used [#30445](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30445) - `include/llama.h`: `llama_batch_ext_set_embd_state` returns false when the context has no state embedding, M-RoPE order documented [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506) - `tools/server`: chat layer refactored around `common_chat_session` with `feed()` / `finish()` [#30210](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30210) - `tools/server`: formatted chat output is now an array of parts instead of a single string [#30389](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30389) - `tools/server`: default listening port changed to 9931 (Docker images keep 8080 inside the container) [#30159](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30159) ### New models - K2 Horizon: dense and MoVA variants with conversion, tokenizer, chat template and `-sm tensor` support [#29535](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29535) - Prism Bonsai 2 27B (ternary) [#29600](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29600) - EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embeddings [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054) - LiquidAI d1-3B and d1-omni-600M decision models [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114) - vLLM decision 2 and vLLM d3 models [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383) - pplx-decider decision model [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044) - MiniCPM-V 4.7 multimodal model [#29416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29416) - Nemotron Super 3.5 VL and Nemotron Bolt 74B A9B [#30520](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30520) - maion-coder architecture [#29778](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29778) - Mellum: MoE gating parameters read from GGUF and unified RoPE handling [#30578](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30578) - LiliCorr draft model conversion and graph [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506) - Rerankers: `classifier_activation` support, exact GELU for ModernBERT encoders [#29692](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29692) [#30108](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30108) ### Core changes - Speculative decoding: MTP for GLM5-Next, LiliCorr drafts, correct mtmd handling in MTP graphs [#29928](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29928) [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506) [#30257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30257) - Speculative decoding: shared nextn tensor flags with consolidated row cropping and sched re-reserve on flag change [#30097](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30097) [#30017](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30017) [#30020](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30020) - Speculative decoding: fixed draft sampling and rejection handling, DFlash output head sharing [#30095](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30095) [#30111](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30111) - New `--spec-draft-n-ubatch` to size the draft context batch separately and save VRAM [#30459](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30459) - MoE expert cache: host-memory experts served from a device LRU cache, supported over multiple GPUs [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887) [#30112](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30112) - Embedding models: skip the logits buffer and the LM head when pooling is enabled (up to 10x less VRAM) [#30255](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30255) [#30445](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30445) - Embedding graphs: reordered `get_rows`, dropped the redundant `t_embd` expand and leftover `ggml_cont` calls [#30160](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30160) [#30461](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30461) [#30198](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30198) - No-cache attention: padded KV dimension and KQ bias, avoided graph reallocations [#30416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30416) [#30446](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30446) [#30439](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30439) - k-pool models: selection built in the causal mask layout, fixed a scatter data race on shared sequences [#30480](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30480) [#29994](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29994) - GLM5-Next sparse attention: removed the gather path [#30042](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30042) - KV cache: honor `LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_PARTIAL_ONLY` so draft checkpoints stop carrying the full KV [#30514](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30514) - Prefetching: merge ranges before issuing system prefetch calls, never map foreign ranges into a backend buffer [#30532](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30532) [#30405](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30405) - Sampling: greedy selection for eligible temperature-zero chains, backend sampling graph kept static across ubatches [#29797](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29797) [#30223](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30223) - Tokenizers: PLaMo-3 pre-segmentation and FiM tokens, opt-in NFC normalization for Unigram, strict UTF-8 validation [#30045](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30045) [#30090](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30090) [#30390](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30390) [#30485](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30485) - Jinja: fixed loop variable scoping, Python-compatible `tojson` rendering, faster context copy [#30533](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30533) [#30483](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30483) [#30362](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30362) [#30562](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30562) - Model split: distribute layers evenly when no device reports free memory [#29677](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29677) ### Multi-modality changes - Added `mtmd_build_inp_attn_mask` for building non-causal multimodal attention masks [#30259](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30259) - Added cohere2 vision encoder support [#30062](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30062) - MTP drafts now handle mtmd inputs, Qwen3.8 Flash Next accepts image embeddings [#30257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30257) [#30397](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30397) - New multimodal architectures: MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL, EmbeddingGemma-2 (vision + audio) [#29416](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29416) [#30520](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30520) [#30054](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30054) ### Server changes - `/v1/systemone` extended to the new decision models: d1-3B, d1-omni, vLLM decision 2/d3, pplx-decider [#30110](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30110) [#30114](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30114) [#30378](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30378) [#30383](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30383) [#30044](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30044) - Chat refactor: session-based parsing and part-based formatted output [#30210](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30210) [#30389](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30389) - Generated text and tokens are now accumulated as parser input, preparing token-aware parsing [#29876](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29876) - Prompt cache: only restorable slot states are saved, so rerank and embedding requests no longer fill the cache [#30498](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30498) - Prompt cache: child tasks prefer empty slots and preserve the state they would overwrite [#30567](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30567) - A pinned busy slot is left untouched until the request can run on it [#30295](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30295) - Slot save/restore now keeps context checkpoints and the draft model state [#26004](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26004) [#30574](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30574) - Fixed an off-by-two in the SWA reuse threshold that discarded restored states [#30580](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30580) - Fixed a stack-overflow crash when escaping special tokens with `std::regex` [#30243](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30243) - `LLAMA_ARG_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` environment variable for `--slot-save-path` [#30272](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30272) - New per-component server tests; vendored cpp-httplib updated to 0.61.0 [#30312](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30312) [#30494](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30494) [#30134](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30134) [#30081](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30081) ### UI changes - New Models Manager: one table of all served models with expandable quants, search, filters, sorting and favorites [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583) - Row actions: load/unload, delete from disk, hide/unhide, resumable downloads with progress [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583) - Model configuration side drawer with model info, chat template and "start a new chat" / "use in this chat" actions [#29583](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583) - Models manager follow-ups: GGUF training context, favorite UX, filter and sort fixes [#30228](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30228) - Fixed `ui_settings` not being applied on the first visit in router mode [#29668](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29668) - Fixed text attachment preview overflow for large pasted text [#29898](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29898) - Fixed the default agentic turns limit falling back to 10 instead of 100 [#30582](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30582) ### ggml changes - ggml updated to [v0.27.0](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.27.0): the backend scheduler gains user callbacks for split weight copying and compute-buffer reallocation, and the RPC protocol is bumped to v8 for tensor-parallel RPC servers. Backends gained chunked gated-delta-net kernels on CUDA/HIP, KleidiAI SME2 k-quant matmuls and AVX2 Q2_0 dot products on CPU, L2-aware coopmat2 scheduling and bf16 activations on Vulkan, reordered-layout MoE kernels (MXFP4, IQ3, Q5_K, grouped XMX GEMM) on SYCL, dp4a MoE GEMMs on OpenCL, tensor-API and wider-head-dim flash attention on Metal, and a DMA/HVX copy overhaul with pooling and 3D im2col ops on Hexagon. Correctness work focused on non-contiguous and strided views, grid and workgroup size limits, out-of-bounds accesses and well-defined `mul_mat_id` behavior for duplicate expert ids; symbol visibility now defaults to hidden ## Assets **Nightly build:** [b11669](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b11669) ## More info - [Releases and versioning of `ggml-org` items.title: Release v5.20.0
items.abstract_or_text: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as ` ` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior. * 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap ## Exporters Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. This makes it easier to export optimized models for efficient inference across different backends. For more information see the docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/exporters_quantization ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. FSDP × TP model and optimizer checkpoints can now be saved and loaded across different parallel configurations, and expert-parallel dispatch, tensor-parallel plans, static-cache `generate()`, and the caching allocator's byte count were fixed. Tied LM heads in composite models now get their own TP plan entry, `enable_expert_parallel` applies the EP plan alone again, TPU loading uses the `tor * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading, Optimizer (#49256) by @michaelbenayoun in [#49256] * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading (#48802) by @michaelbenayoun in [#48802] * Don't set a device per rank for gloo tensor-parallel tests (#49636) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49636] * fix(distributed): keep enable_expert_parallel as EP alone (#49633) by @dacorvo in [#49633] * Fix a port allocation race in FSDP tests (#49455) by @icavan in [#49455] * Expert-parallel dispatch hands the experts the received rows, not the all-to-all's pending result (#49421) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49421] * Fix static-cache generate() with host-side inputs and under TP (#49317) by @dacorvo in [#49317] * Composite lm head tp plan (#49080) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49080] * Fix: use torch.accelerator device APIs so TP loading works again on TPU (#49502) by @tengomucho in [#49502] * Count ep and fsdp in caching_allocator_warmup byte calculation (#49384) by @3outeille in [#49384] * Do not wrap the model in FSDP for expert-parallel token dispatch (#49383) by @3outeille in [#49383] ## Generation This release fixes static-cache `generate()` bugs with host-side inputs and under tensor parallelism. It also speeds up Whisper generation on TPU by cutting device syncs and recompilation, and fixes Whisper batched timestamp decoding for tensor and NumPy inputs. Pipelines get a cleanup of generation-argument handling that removes spurious warnings. * Add job to automatically generate Intel CPU Docker image (#49560) by @regisss in [#49560] * Image decoding moves to torchcodec (#47963) by @zucchini-nlp in [#47963] * Optimize Whisper generation for TPU and device sync (#49426) by @tengomucho in [#49426] * Generation cleanup in pipelines (#49269) by @Rocketknight1 in [#49269] * Fix Whisper batch timestamp decoding for tensors (#49419) by @Kingofbooks in [#49419] ## Vision Vision processing was updated in several places. Image decoding now uses torchcodec, Molmo2's image and video kwargs follow the library's standard conventions, and Pixtral Flash Attention no longer detects false image boundaries after the axial RoPE refactor, which had caused CUDA illegal memory access errors and incorrect output. Several CI and Docker changes also shipped: GPU images moved to Python 3.11, a numpy/pyarrow conflict * Fix numpy/pyarrow conflict in the XPU Docker image (#49582) by @jiqing-feng in [#49582] * CI: Move GPU images to python 3.11 (#49352) by @tarekziade in [#49352] * Update molmo2 processing images/videos kwargs (#49563) by @guarin in [#49563] * Fix Pixtral Flash Attention image boundaries after axial RoPE refactor (#49373) by @oliverholworthy in [#49373] ## Kernels This release improves kernel support across hardware. `flash_attention_2` now falls back to the AITER kernel on ROCm when `flash-attn` isn't installed, and T5-style models get a contiguous SDPA position-bias mask so they use fused kernels again. The Hub rotary kernel is now limited to CUDA inference because its backward pass gave incorrect gradients. The Atlas Inference Gated DeltaNet kernels for Strix Halo and * Fall back to the AITER kernel for flash_attention_2 on ROCm (#49608) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in [#49608] * Make the SDPA position_bias mask contiguous so T5-style models use fused kernels (#49517) by @IvenHsu01 in [#49517] * Use the Hub rotary kernel for inference only on CUDA (#49439) by @qgallouedec in [#49439] * [Atlas Inference] Enable torch.compile for the Strix Halo Gated DeltaNet hub kernel (#49453) by @AzeezIsh in [#49453] * [Atlas Inference] Fix GB10 Gated DeltaNet hub kernel for transformers 5.17+ and enable torch.compile (#49452) by @AzeezIsh in [#49452] ## Cache This release fixes several cache-related bugs: static-cache `generate()` now handles host-side nested inputs and tensor parallelism correctly, the offloaded cache prefetch no longer races with the offloading copy, and Phi3 LongRoPE cache rebuilds at the context boundary now receive the full prefix. It also counts the query token in MiMo-V2-Flash's sliding window and corrects the quantized cache (hqq/quanto) documentation exam * Fix offloaded cache prefetch racing with the offloading copy items.title: v1.16.0
items.abstract_or_text: ## Features ### 🛠️ TRL now trains on AWS Trainium The fused LM head from v1.15 is what made Neuron tractable; the remaining gaps are closed here. There is a [guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/neuron) to go with it. Neuron recompiles once per input shape, so an unpadded run stalls about a minute on every new sequence length. `pad_to_multiple_of` now defaults to `"auto"`: 128 on Neuron, `None` elsewhere, so nothing changes on GPU. Trainium2, Qwen3-0.6B SFT, 20 steps: **130 s with the default against 260 s without**. * Add a guide for training on AWS Trainium by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7729 * Default `pad_to_multiple_of` to `"auto"` by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7724 * Run the fused LM head and distillation kernels on devices without Triton by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7669 * Report the Neuron device in `trl env` and telemetry by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7672 * Support any accelerator in activation offloading by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7670 ### 🌳 Tree attention for AsyncGRPO AsyncGRPO now packs every micro-batch row as a **prefix tree** instead of a flat sequence. Multi-turn and multi-generation rollouts repeat a lot of prefix: on a shared prompt, those tokens used to be forwarded once per row. Tree packing forwards them once. ```text rollout 0: [ prompt ] [ completion A ] prompt ──┬── completion A ── later turn rollout 1: [ prompt ] [ completion B ] => └── completion B rollout 2: [ prompt ] [ completion A ] [ … ] ``` Chains without a fork collapse into segments, and each segment's queries attend to the K/V gathered along its root-to-segment path in a single FA3 varlen call. No mask tensor: every layer except attention runs once per unique token, and only K/V is duplicated along shared prefixes. Qwen3-1.7B, 32K tokens per rollout, forward + backward: | layout | packing ratio | sequence packing | tree packing | peak GiB | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | shared prompt | 1.00 | 8677 ms | 8737 ms (0.99×) | 35.2 → 35.2 | | shared prompt | 2.29 | 8266 ms | **4341 ms (1.90×)** | 35.2 → 18.0 | | shared prompt | 3.37 | 8179 ms | **2755 ms (2.97×)** | 35.2 → 13.6 | | nested fork | 1.60 | 8557 ms | 6217 ms (1.38×) | 35.2 → 23.8 | | nested fork | 3.56 | 8172 ms | **2635 ms (3.10×)** | 35.2 → 13.5 | There is no `packing` option to choose: with nothing shared a tree row is exactly the old sequence packing, at a ~1% cost. by @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7328 ### Muse Spark Open Support for [`meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B`](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B): the tiny-model script, coverage in the VLM tests (SFT, DPO, KTO, chat-template utils, fused LM head), and a LoRA SFT example on 8 nodes of 8×H100 with `DistributedConfig(fsdp_size=64, ep_size=8)`, token dispatch and packing. Measured at **14.2 s/step, 131k tokens/step, 40.2 GB per GPU**. Needs `transformers>=5.20.0`; the adapter save additionally needs [transformers#49500](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49500) with peft 0.21.2. by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7536 ### AMD GPUs in the async trainers * Support AMD GPUs in the async GRPO and async distillation trainers by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7689 * Hide the GPU from the async rollout worker on ROCm by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7685 ### Tool-call arguments typed by the tool's JSON schema `parse_response` now receives the tools, so tool-call arguments come back typed from the tool's own schema instead of whatever the raw parse produced. by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7650 ### Other * Async GRPO tool metrics by @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7624 * Store async GRPO and distillation rollout sample tokens as numpy arrays by @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7626 * Save the final step when async trainers stop at `num_train_epochs` by @lewtun in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7628 * Pass sequence boundaries from the padding-free collator by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7599 * Build the reference model with the policy's dtype and attention implementation by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7597, and the SDFT/SDPO teacher with the student's by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7616 * Find unused parameters under DDP for vision-language models by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7598 * Pad the generation prompts to `pad_to_multiple_of` by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7671 * Drop the client-side observe loop from the CARLA examples by @sergiopaniego in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7721 * Use `None` for unscored `env.reward` in OpenReward by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7541 ### Removals and requirement bumps * **Remove the experimental SSD trainer** by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7706 * **Refuse `nn.DataParallel` in `RewardTrainer`** by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7571 * Drop vLLM 0.21.0 support by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7700 * Require `accelerate>=1.10.1` and drop the `ParallelismConfig` shim by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7643 * Declare a minimum bitsandbytes version by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7641 * Declare the direct dependencies TRL gets transitively by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7713 ## Fixes * **Fix silently wrong `torch.compile` results in the Triton loss kernels on torch < 2.11.** `torch_compile=True` trained with `loss=0.0` and `grad_norm=nan` at every step. Inductor passes scalar kernel args as `constexpr` before torch 2.11, the `.to(tl.float32)` casts raised on those, and Inductor then assumed every input was mutated and miscompiled. By @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7688 * **Fix FSDP2 vLLM colocate weight sync for tied-embedding models** by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7647 * **Prevent VLM policies from generating the image placeholder token** in GRPO, RLOO and Distillation by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7695 * **Fix Online DPO VLM training** when the prompt exceeds `max_length` (https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7703) and for processors with 5D pixel values (https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7704), both by @albertvillanova * **Fix activation offloading on torch < 2.4** by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7748 * Fix `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` of `selective_log_softmax_and_entropy` on torch 2.6 by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7719 * Keep the Triton loss kernels in fp32 under `torch.compile` by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7600 * Read `is_triton_available` once in the fused LM head kernels so Dynamo does not warn by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7731 * Fix Distillation for models split across devices by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7573 * Restore the gradient checkpointing kwargs after generation by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7668 * Drop the FlashAttention warnings for padding-free and packing in SFT by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7620 * Restore the distributed env vars that vLLM colocate tests leave behind by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7723 ### Clearer errors A sweep making failure modes explicit instead of crashing deep in the stack, all by @albertvillanova: * Raise a clear error when the fused LM head is used without Triton (#7639) * Raise a clear error for prefix tuning on peft versions that cannot support it (#7646) * Raise a clear error when the Distillation student and teacher heads are on different devices (#7605) * Reject a text-only teacher in GOLD VLM distillation instead of crashing (#7581) * Name the missing vLLM server setting when the server cannot serve TRL (#7611) * Raise early for `use_kernels` with transformers 5.2.0 and 5.3.0 (#7577), and if kernels is installed with transformers 5.3.0 in the tiny NemotronH scripts (#7575) ## Documentation * Add a guide for training on AWS Trainium by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7729 * Add guidance on testing through the public API to the contributing guide and agent instructions by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7606 * Document the criterion for raising a dependency version floor by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7638 ## CI **Real objects, not mocks.** The bulk of this cycle, applying the repo's testing rule across the suite, all by @albertvillanova: run the GRPO entropy mask tests on a real trainer instead of a Mock (#7566), the teacher logprob tests on a real trainer instead of a MagicMock (#7579), build real GOLD trainers in the init (#7582), input preparation (#7614), on-policy generation (#7613, #7615), output decoding (#7633), ULD helper (#7634) and no-backend tokenizer (#7635) tests, check GOLD dataset preparation through the trainer (#7632), and build real async trainers in the rollout state checkpoint tests (#7583) **Coverage**, all by @albertvillanova: test SFT (#7552) and DPO/KTO/Reward/GRPO/RLOO (#7601) on a model split across devices, test fp16 training across six trainers (#7572) **Experimental suite on main**, all by @albertvillanova: run the experimental tests on pushes to main (#7675), nightly (#7681), on demand (#7678) and when their Makefile target or dependencies change (#7680), and report failures to Slack (#7676) **Other**: use Python 3.13 by default in CI by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7648, remove the slow test infrastructure (#7604), rename the distributed smoke tests to distributed tests (#7631), skip the kernel tests when Triton is not installed (#7563), guard the aiohttp import in the experimental async rollout workers (#7578), drop `use_cpu` and `bf16` settings the CPU fixture already covers (#7612), re-record the `sft_fa2` invariant reference after the fused LM head by @qgallouedec (#7591), plus warning filters in #7586, #7588, #7590, #7645, #7727 ## New Contributors * @Abdennacer-Badaoui made their first contribution in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7647 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/compare/v1.15.0...v1.16.0

## New Features - Open `/config` to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart. (#52990, #53429) - Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately. Interrupting a turn also stops active Code Mode cells and their nested tool calls. (#51812, #51835) - Configure a leader key in `/keymap`. The default is `Ctrl+X`, shortcut hints stay open until you choose or cancel, and voice mute moves to `F9`. (#52273) - Restart a managed background server from `/daemon`. Codex warns about work the restart could interrupt, then reconnects automatically. (#53173) - Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups. (#52245) - Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts. `codex exec` can also select it with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access. (#53701, #53717) ## Bug Fixes - Resuming a saved thread restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy. (#53150, #53419, #53424) - The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate `Host` headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks. (#51650, #52661, #53506) - Return to an existing side conversation with `/side` after switching threads. Answers to pending prompts also go back to the thread that asked. (#52184, #53436) - On Windows, `Ctrl+V` and `Shift+Insert` paste text as well as images. On WSL, repeated pastes reuse the clipboard reader, and copy attempts time out instead of hanging. (#53224, #52967, #53453) - Local commands finish promptly when a child keeps an output pipe open. Remote commands preserve late-arriving output so the final poll can still collect it. (#52652, #53331, #53622) - `codex exec` no longer prints the same file diff again after an unrelated command. (#53444) ## Documentation - Updated the bundled OpenAI Docs guidance for migrations to the GPT-6 family, including model-specific reasoning, tool use, and data residency considerations. (#51768) - Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering. (#52610) ## Chores - Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched `zsh`. Configurations using the retired shell flags receive a migration notice. (#52160, #52213) - Reduced Linux and macOS release package size by stripping symbols from packaged binaries while preserving them in the original build outputs. items.abstract_or_text: ## NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super [NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super](https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3.5-super) is a vision-language model for coding, reasoning, tool use, and document understanding. It pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mamba-2/Transformer mixture-of-experts backbone (12B active per token) with a C-RADIO vision encoder, and supports tool calling, an on/off thinking mode, and context up to 1M tokens. ``` ollama run nemotron-3.5-super ``` A compact sibling, [Nemotron 3.5 Bolt](https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3.5-bolt), distills Super down to 74B parameters (9B active) tuned to fit a 24 GB NVIDIA GPU for everyday agentic tasks, with speculative decoding via its included drafter. ## What's Changed * Decision models are now available on cloud — use `clef:cloud` and `clef-flash:cloud` to run decision models through ollama.com cloud without pulling them locally * Continuing an OpenAI-compatible Responses conversation that includes custom tool calls no longer fails with an error * Clearer error messages when cloud access fails: sign-in problems, payment issues in the desktop app, and upstream access errors from the ChatGPT gateway now explain what went wrong * Updated llama.cpp (adding Nemotron 3.5 support) and MLX ## New Contributors * @willietran made their first contribution in https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18986 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.4...v0.40.5

items.title: v0.40.4
items.abstract_or_text: ## Decision models in the CLI Decision models can now be used directly from the terminal with `ollama run` — ask yes/no questions, classify text into labels, or score against a rubric: `ollama run nimble --ask "Is a refund being requested?" < ticket.txt` ## What's Changed * Kev decision models are now supported by the MLX runner on Apple silicon * `ollama launch` can now be used with usage credits without upgrading to a paid plan * `ollama launch codex` now includes locally installed Ollama models in its model picker. Use `/model` within the Codex CLI to swap models. * Improved inference performance by reusing verified manifests and already loaded models * Added support for multimodal embeddings through llama-server * Fixed loading multimodal embedding models with small context windows * Improved Gemma 4 prefill performance on NVIDIA GPUs with the MLX runner * MLX runner now clips long Laya states instead of rejecting them * Improved speculative decoding reliability in the MLX runner, including recurrent state handling after rollback * Updated llama.cpp with native decision model support * Updated README and documentation with clearer privacy and cloud-services wording **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.3...v0.40.4

items.abstract_or_text: vulkan : copy strided f16 KV once on AMD so reads spread across memory channels (#27703) * vulkan : copy strided f16 KV once so reads spread across memory channels Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 4.8 / Opus 5) * tests : cover the f16 KV copy to scratch Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 4.8 / Opus 5) * vulkan : gate the f16 KV scratch copy to AMD Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 4.8 / Opus 5) * vulkan : reuse the generic copy shader for the f16 KV scratch fill The f16 clause needs only a strided copy, not a dequant, so drop the dedicated shader and dispatch the existing copy pipeline instead. The copy is described in source memory order so the strided access lands on the writes, which stream, instead of the reads, which would concentrate on a few memory channels. Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 4.8 / Opus 5 / Fable 5) * vulkan : extend the strided KV scratch copy to bf16 Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5 * vulkan : clean up comments Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5 * consolidate copy shaders * disable on RDNA4 --------- Co-authored-by: Ruben Ortlam **Website:** - items.title: b11642
items.abstract_or_text: server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache (#30498) * server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache The idle-slot save loop stores every idle slot whenever a task starts, while only completion tasks restore from the prompt cache. Rerank, embedding, decision and infill states fill the cache up to its limit without ever being read back, and slots already cached are offered again at every task start. Each slot now tracks with cache_pending whether its state is restorable and missing from the cache: a completion release or an explicit slot restore sets it, prompt_save consumes it, prompt_clear resets it. Both save paths share this rule, and the LRU path restores only for completion tasks. * server: test that decision slots skip the prompt cache Decision tasks never mark their slot as cacheable, so starting new tasks must not save their idle slots to the RAM prompt cache, with or without a unified KV cache. * server: restore any reusing task from the prompt cache Embedding and rerank tasks never reuse their state, so their slots are cleared on release like child slots and the cache only holds states that a later task can restore. Infill and decision tasks now restore from the cache too, which replaces the cache_pending flag. Decision models disable the prompt cache unless --cache-ram is given, since their states seldom repeat. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11642/llama-b11642-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: sycl: IQ3 code reorder (#29107) * sycl: persistent IQ3_S/IQ3_XXS weight reorder for SYCL decode and prefill Add persistent reordered weight layouts for IQ3_S and IQ3_XXS. Weights are reordered once at load time; the reordered MMVQ dot products then walk dense super-blocks with dp4a and SWAR sign expansion instead of gathering bits from the interleaved standard layout. Reorder-aware dequantization feeds the batched prefill GEMMs so prompt processing sees the same benefit. Also harden the oneDNN build check: a missing DNNL package or a CPU-only DNNL build now fails at configure time instead of silently producing a degraded backend. Measured on Intel Arc Pro B70 with Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S (MTP), -ngl 999 -b 4096 -ub 1024 -fa on: tg256 @ 0 ctx 12.92 -> 23.54 tok/s (+82%) tg256 @ 9,216 12.33 -> 21.69 tok/s (+76%) tg256 @ 64,000 9.76 -> 14.91 tok/s (+53%) pp8192 833.9 -> 833.6 tok/s (flat) Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M / Q3_K_M are unchanged within noise (largest delta -0.5% pp, tg flat), so standard quants are not affected. The MMVQ GLU fusion widening and rms_norm+scale fusion are intentionally not part of this change; master already carries them via #28931. * removing wait as per review request * sycl : fix fusion.cpp line ending **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input (#28738) * ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input The GEMM behind conv_1d folds the batch into its rows, so the product sits in memory as [OL, N, OC] while the reshape claims [OL, OC, N]. The shape is right and the contents are transposed, so nothing fires: no assert, no abort, the graph just runs and the channels come out interleaved with the batches. With N == 1 the two readings describe the same buffer, which is why the three vocoders in the tree never hit it, they all squeeze to 2d right after the call. Reshape to the real layout and permute OC and N back. The N == 1 path keeps its direct reshape, so the current callers build the same graph and pay for no extra copy. tests/test-conv-1d.cpp compares one batched convolution against N single batch convolutions built from the same weight and the same input slices. Five of the seven geometries fail before this change and all seven pass after. N == 1 and OC == 1 pass either way, since swapping two dimensions when one of them is 1 changes nothing. The batched path matters to downstream audio projects where several synthesis lanes share a single graph. Nothing in mtmd batches a vocoder today, each one streams one flow and carries its left context between calls, but the op is correct now if one of them grows a lane dimension. * ggml: build the same conv_1d graph for every batch size Address review from ggerganov: drop the N == 1 branch of ggml_conv_1d. The GEMM result is always reshaped to [OC, N, OL] and permuted back, as ggml_conv_2d does, so every batch size builds the same graph. For N == 1 this adds a cont on an already ordered tensor. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11630/llama-b11630-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) -
